title: Date and setting of the picture at Racket Park
summary: They date the photo before 1916 and Arthur says it was taken at a picnic at Racket Park, where a lacrosse-like game was played; guitarist unknown.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You can shut this off at any time when you have to. Hey, we're talking about that photograph of the Peerless band. Yeah. Well, Ab Frank isn't on there, I guess, a piccolo player, is there? I don't think.
No.

I understood that he was one of the leaders at one time at around 1906 or some such time. Have you any idea on the date of that? Of this picture? Yes. You can tell maybe a little bit about how old your father looks since he died in 1916. Did he look something like that as you remember it? Oh yeah, yeah.

He just liked that when he died, yeah, during 1916. But this picture was way a little while before he died. A little while earlier than that you think of? Yeah, yeah, way before he died. This was when they had this, this park was an old park they had back, if I'm not mistaken, around the old Racket Green.
Maybe I don't know where that is either. I can't see.
Well that was, let's see where we had prayer. The Racket Green was back here, back around the Bayer, the old Bayer.
Bayer St. John, out that way. Yeah.
They had a Racket Green and that's where they were playing at. This was at the Racket Green when they played this. This was a picnic I think.
What do they do at the Racket Green? What kind of games did they have?
They played that game, some kind of a racket. They used to play the regular racket game they had.
The racket's like tennis rackets or something?

Yeah, that's something they catch with the two sticks and pitchets. I don't know much about the game because I was a very young kid, you know, I didn't know much about it. But they used to play that racket back in this park and that's why they call it the Racket Green. You see, because they used to play the game back then. They had a picnic out there and that's where they played that Sunday. See, they were all sitting around a tree playing.
I never noticed much about this picture. It is right out there. Yeah, it's right outdoors then. I thought maybe it was a, oh sure, it's a big bench there. Yeah, they're out in the park.
They're out in the park. That's the Racket Green they're playing in.
Sure.
Sometimes... You know, the Racket Park?

No, no. The Racket Park. That's where it's at. Racket Park. That's what it's called. Yeah. And they used to have that game they called Racket. They used to play. I don't know, somehow or another you catch a ball or something with two sticks and throw it and I don't know how they played it.
Sounds like lacrosse. It's been saying something like lacrosse. Yeah, well I don't know much about the game.
I was such a small kid. I don't guess I had it played or nothing but I've heard of it.
I think I read something about the game. You don't know who the guitar player is, I forget now.
Yeah, that's a fella. I never could know who that guy was either. I don't remember this little fella.

Supposed to be one fella, Coochie Martin, that played with the Peerless Band at one period. He was a brother, there was another Henry Martin who played drums too. Their mother took care of a school up there on Perdido Street. Remember in Louis Armstrong's neighborhood up there right there? Yeah, yeah, yeah.
I remember the school you're speaking about.
And this Mrs. Martin, he even 20 years ago.

This fella here, I don't remember him at all. I remember everybody on this picture, but this little guy thought for them. But these two fellas, I just remember their names. It was hard for me to remember. I was such a young kid when all this was going on.
